paper_title: More Tokens, Lower Precision Towards the Optimal Token-Precision   Trade-off in KV Cache Compression
caption: The results of Layer-Wise Quantized Pruning on Mistral-7B-v0.2-Instruct, with SnapKV as pruning method. KV cache budget=1/64.
model_annotation: The line plot illustrates the relative change in performance across different transformer layers when applying layer-wise quantized pruning to the Mistral-7B-v0.2-Instruct model using the SnapKV method, under a KV cache budget of 1/64. The x-axis represents grouped transformer layers — Layer1-4, Layer5-12, Layer13-20, Layer21-28, and Layer29-32 — with no numerical scale, while the y-axis shows the “Relative Change” as a percentage, ranging from -25% to +5%, with major gridlines at 5% intervals. Five distinct lines are plotted: a yellow line with circle markers for “LB-Avg of 2×tokens,8-bit” starts near 0%, dips slightly to ~-2% at Layer5-12, then rises to ~0% at Layer29-32; a red line with square markers for “LB-Avg of 1×tokens,16-bit” begins near 0%, drops to ~-5% at Layer5-12, recovers to ~-2% at Layer13-20, and ends near 0%; a light blue line with circle markers for “RULER4k of 2×tokens,8-bit” starts near -2%, dips to ~-13% at Layer13-20, then rebounds to ~-2% at Layer29-32; a dark blue line with square markers for “RULER4k of 1×tokens,16-bit” begins near -4%, plummets to -25% at Layer13-20, then recovers to ~-5% at Layer29-32; and a gray dashed line labeled “Baseline of 4×tokens,4-bit” remains flat at 0% across all layers, serving as the reference point. All lines show significant dips in the middle layers (especially Layer13-20), with recovery toward the final layers, indicating layer-dependent sensitivity to quantization and token count.
